Fixes alkem-io/server#6329

Server half of the removal fix; the Matrix half is alkem-io/matrix-adapter#82. Part of epic alkem-io/alkemio#1801 (Phase 1).

## Root cause

Removing a member from a group conversation deleted the Alkemio membership, but the Matrix kick was always rejected: every member holds the same power level, so nobody outranks anybody. The removed user stayed `join` in Synapse, kept receiving messages and could still post. Server side, three gaps made this worse:
- The "fall back to local removal only if the workflow threw" branch could never run: the event emitter logs a failing `room.member.updated` listener instead of rethrowing, so a failed workflow left the membership in place.
- A removal completed locally after a failed or timed-out RPC was later confirmed by Matrix's own leave, which published `MEMBER_REMOVED` a second time (and could delete the conversation twice).
- Room deletion removes the row before the Matrix room, so every member's later leave hit a room that no longer exists.

## Fix

- `completeLocalMemberRemoval` always ends with the idempotent row deletion.
- `handleConversationMemberLeft` acts only when its call actually removed the row (`persistMemberRemoved` now reports it), so a late leave is a no-op.
- `handleRoomMemberUpdated` ignores events for rooms that no longer exist (new `RoomLookupService.getRoom`).
- RPC transport failures (timeouts) take the local-removal path, as they already did; comments, the warning text and the docs now say so.
- `removeConversationMember` / `leaveConversation` GraphQL descriptions updated; `schema.graphql` regenerated (descriptions only).
- `docs/matrix-admin-reflection.md` Finding 1 rewritten for the new mechanism and its limits.

## Regression tests

- `message.inbox.service.spec.ts`: stale leave for a deleted room is ignored; a late leave after local removal publishes nothing.
- `conversation.service.spec.ts`, `conversation.resolver.mutations.spec.ts`: local removal always completes; rejected/timed-out removal paths.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest run src/domain/communication/conversation` 76 passed; `message.inbox.service.spec` 25 passed.

## Verified end to end (local stack, this branch + alkem-io/matrix-adapter#82)

Before (develop): after removal B stayed `join` in Synapse, still received new messages and could send (event accepted); server log `Matrix kick rejected`.
After: B's own account leaves (`leave`, sender = B), new messages are not visible to B, B's send is rejected with `M_FORBIDDEN`, no "kick rejected" warning, `MEMBER_REMOVED` published once; voluntary leave and last-member auto-delete still work. Not run live: space-member removal and an adapter timeout during removal (covered by unit tests).

Adds a **Form** Post framing: an admin-only Post whose questions sit in the framing. ## What

Adds the server half of in-app SSO: app mode is decided at `GET /api/auth/oidc/login` from an `app_challenge`, carried stickily in the signed pre-auth cookie across Kratos' query-less re-entry, and a new `GET /api/auth/oidc/app-handoff` mints the WebView's session from a single-use ≤60s Redis code.

- `app-redirect-scheme.ts` — frozen host→scheme map (no config key, anchored so `io.alkem.app` cannot match `io.alkem.app.sandbox`)
- `app-handoff.redis.ts` — the one-shot GETDEL code store; `created_at` pinned to the code's issue time so revocation still wins
- `/callback` in app mode establishes **nothing** in the auth-browser jar, clears the Kratos cookie with the full `{name, domain, path, maxAge}` quad, and 302s into the app scheme — as do the three post-cookie rejection sites (`state_mismatch`, `token_exchange_failed`, `nonce_mismatch`)
- `/app-handoff` cannot throw: both awaits guarded, closed five-member error set, every failure to `/login?app_signin=failed`
- `audit.ts` gains exactly one member; `constants.ts` gains only `APP_VERIFIER_HEADER`; **`returnto-validator.ts` untouched**

## Why

Today the hop to an external IdP leaves the WebView, so the session lands in the browser's cookie jar where the WebView can never read it and the app stays signed out. Observed on device 2026-07-29. See alkem-io/server#6340 for the full analysis.

## Tests

`pnpm typecheck:native` clean; **28 files / 317 tests** in `src/core/auth/oidc` + `test/integration/oidc`. Full repo suite green (836 files / 10,671 tests). Includes two in-process supertest integration specs and a spying-logger test proving no verifier, code or handoff URL is ever logged.

---

## Workspace feature

`workspace#079-app-sso-handoff` — spec, plan, per-repo tasks and ADR `0016-app-native-session-handoff-contract.md` live in `agents-hq` at `specs/079-app-sso-handoff/`. Implements alkem-io/server#6340 (Phase 2 only; Phase 1 provider-hiding was explicitly rejected).

## Design in one paragraph

The whole authentication chain runs in a **real browser** (`ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, Chrome Custom Tab on Android), which satisfies every IdP's embedded-WebView policy and keeps Kratos CSRF, Hydra and pre-auth cookies in one consistent jar. The session is handed back into the WebView **once, server-side**, through a single-use ≤60s Redis code redeemed with a verifier in the `X-Alkemio-App-Verifier` request header. **Tokens never leave the server.** App mode is decided at `/login` (not `/callback`) and made sticky in the signed pre-auth cookie — mandatory, because Kratos' `registration.after.oidc` re-enters a *bare* `/api/auth/oidc/login` with no query string, so a query-param-only flag is provably lost on the social sign-up leg. The redirect scheme is **derived** from a frozen host map, not configured, so no infra change ships with this. `returnto-validator.ts` is untouched.

## Evidence digest

| Stage | Result |
|---|---|
| Triage | routed `spec`; 7 of 9 premise claims confirmed against real code, 2 escalated and then closed by the operator |
| Spec review | attempt 1 stopped at `revise-exhausted` (40→38 findings, 27 blocking both rounds). Re-architected smaller under 4 operator mandates. Attempt 2 converged **23 → 16 → 13 blocking, zero HIGH**; 13 mediums knowingly accepted as tracked spec debt |
| Simplification | 18 lines removed across 3 items, repo gates green before and after |
| Cross-repo contracts | 3/3 pass (`app-handoff-wire`, `app-signin-landing-params`, `redirect-scheme-matches-app-id`) |
| **Live verification** | **`not-applicable` — NO stack was booted and NO acceptance walk was run.** `server/quickstart-services.yml` pins 24 `container_name` values `docker compose -p` cannot namespace, so an isolated stack would stack-conflict or collide with a developer's dev stack. Executed evidence is the per-repo gates plus two in-process supertest integration specs |
| Review funnel | 34 raw → 32 in-diff → 25 confirmed → **14 actionable**, 7 refuted with verbatim source citations |
| Fixes | **13 of 14 fixed**, scoped confirm pass over the fix hunks, **0 regressions** |
| Security verdict | **conditional** on all three repos, with one accepted high (below) |

## ⚠️ Accepted risk — SEC-079-01 (high, operator-attested)

**A malicious Android app squatting the `io.alkem.app` private-use scheme can redeem a full `alkemio_session`** — including a refresh token with `offline_access` — for a victim who holds a live `ory_kratos_session` in Chrome's jar. The PKCE-shaped verifier/challenge binding defeats *interception* of a legitimate flow but gives nothing against a flow **the attacker itself initiated**, because the attacker chose the challenge. Before this change a hostile local app could at most mint a session in Chrome's own jar, which its sandbox cannot read; the handoff converts that into a redeemable bearer credential.

The adjudicator **refused** a proposed downgrade to medium. Accepted by **@bobbykolev** on 2026-09-29 to unblock shipping, tracked as **alkem-io/server#6545**. Narrowing preconditions: the attacker app must be installed; the victim must hold that Chrome Kratos session (a legitimate in-app sign-in clears it); **Android only**, since iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession` is ephemeral. SOC 2 CC6.1/CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.5.17/A.8.5.

## Other tracked residuals

- **No end-to-end proof of any user-visible flow.** Per-provider × per-platform sign-in (Microsoft, LinkedIn, GitHub, Cleverbase on iOS + Android) remains an **unsigned human device-matrix gate** in `client-appstore/docs/go-no-go.md`.
- 13 medium spec findings accepted before implementation (device-matrix rows for two success criteria, `verifier_missing` having no producer, the iOS cold-start branch being Android-only by construction, and a Swift string-literal style constraint).
- 2 baseline findings reported, non-blocking — they are pre-existing debt, not introduced here.
- The `scope:client-appstore` review agent died mid-response, so **that repo's diff scoping may be incomplete**; its findings were still produced and fixed, but full coverage is not claimed.
- Implementer-flagged, deliberately not hardened: on the `session_establish_failed` path `regenerate()` has already succeeded when `save()` rejects, so express-session may persist a valid session while the user lands on `/login?app_signin=failed`. Not a privilege issue — the session belongs to whoever just authenticated.

## Merge coordination

Draft PRs #6541 and #6542 (both already CONFLICTING against `develop`, idle since 2026-09-25) touch `src/core/auth/oidc/audit.ts`, `oidc-core.module.ts` and `strategies/cookie-session.strategy.ts`. This work edited **`audit.ts` only**, adding one enum member. Nothing was pre-merged.

Fixes #6536.

## What went wrong

Every conversion and move mutation is gated on an in-memory policy built in the `ConversionResolverMutations` constructor. Its role list is the entire check — the policy is in-memory, so no credential rule in the database can widen it.

`67bc7945f` ("initial pass at updating global roles", May 2024) renamed the global role `global-admin-spaces` to `global-support`. Throughout that commit the symbol was renamed in place and kept in its lists:

```diff
-  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
+  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_SUPPORT,
```

At this one call site it was deleted instead of renamed:

```diff
-    [
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN,
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
-    ],
+    [AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN],
```

Holders of the role now called `global-support` silently lost access to all seven mutations sharing this policy: `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `convertSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertVirtualContributorToUseKnowledgeBase`.

It reads as a rename that missed a call site rather than a deliberate restriction — nothing in that commit suggests an intent to narrow conversions. **If the narrowing was intentional, this PR should be closed and #6536 answered instead**; I could not find anything recording that intent.

## What this changes

Restores `GLOBAL_SUPPORT` to the role list, and adds a test asserting the list. Nothing covered it before, which is exactly why the rename went unnoticed — the existing specs mock `grantAccessOrFail`, so they pass whatever the roles are.

This also realigns the gate with `createPlatformCredentialRules`, which grants `PLATFORM_ADMIN` to `global-admin`, `global-support` and `global-license-manager`. Before this change a caller could hold `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on the platform and still be refused here.

## Verification

- `vitest run conversion.resolver.mutations.spec.ts` — 20 passed.
- Negative control: reverting the one-line source change fails the new test with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ [ 'global-admin', …(1) ], …(2) ]`, so it does guard the regression.
- `biome check` clean on both files.

## Deliberately left out

Two things surfaced in #6536 that made this hard to diagnose but are separate changes:

- `global-license-manager` also holds `PLATFORM_ADMIN` platform-side but is not in this list. I have not added it — widening beyond restoring the lost role is a product call, not a regression fix.
- The failure logs `on authorization undefined of type 'in-memory'`, which reads like a missing policy and sends you looking in the database. The policy name is already passed to the constructor and would point straight at the real check.

## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

## What actually changed in production code

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. That is the property to verify when reviewing this hunk, and it is why the restructure is called out here instead of being described as an addition.

**`ai.persona.service.ts` — two conditions changed.** `input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT` became `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES.includes(input.engine)`; that is the feature. A second condition was *tightened*: `if (!invocationGraph)` became `if (!invocationGraph && input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT)`, deliberately keeping the default-graph fallback expert-only so a generic persona with no stored graph produces **no `promptGraph` key at all** rather than inheriting expert's default.

**`prompt.graph.node.dto.ts` / `prompt.graph.edge.dto.ts` / `ai.persona.dto.update.ts`** add nullable fields; the only removal is an import line being widened.

Genuinely additive: every new test file, the docs, and the fixture. **No pre-existing test was modified or deleted** (`git diff origin/develop..HEAD -- '**/*.spec.ts' | grep -c '^-'` = 0), and the **GraphQL schema** delta is additive — 21 added, 0 breaking.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The story said "GENERIC"; there is no such enum value.** It is `AiPersonaEngine.GENERIC_OPENAI` (`generic-openai`) — the routing key bound to the `virtual-contributor-engine-generic` queue.
- **The allowlist deliberately excludes** `guidance`, `openai-assistant`, `libra-flow`, `community-manager`: widening requires engine-side graph execution first. A future enum value defaults to *not* attaching.
- **No validation of the graph/body-of-knowledge pairing.** `bodyOfKnowledgeID` is per-invocation from the VC, not stored on the persona, so the server cannot validate it. A retrieve-bearing graph on a BoK-less persona hard-fails at engine parse time and the member sees the standard error response — a documented precondition, not a defect.
- **No migration**: `ai_persona.promptGraph` jsonb already existed engine-independently.
- Expert behaviour is byte-identical in all three modes (stored / default / none).

## Evidence

- **8170 tests pass / 711 files**. Lint, typecheck, build clean.
- `AiPersonaInvocationInput` remains **absent** from `schema.graphql` (count 0).
- The authoring fixture parses through the **actual merged VC engine parser** (`2920c83`): 8 nodes, 2 conditional edges, state model built.

## Review round (8 findings, all fixed, 0 declined)

Two independent reviewers on different providers found non-overlapping defects:

**Security** (verdict was `conditional`, now remediated):
- `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` wrote **no audit record** — a global admin could change the graph governing prompts, retrieval and member output with no attributable trace. Now audits success *and* failure with actor / persona / engine / `promptGraphChanged` only; never the graph, prompt text or credentials (SOC 2 CC7.2·CC7.3, ISO A.8.15·A.8.16). **This is what motivated the resolver restructure described above.**
- The activation guide didn't disclose that retrieve nodes send body-of-knowledge content to the **external model provider**; it now requires a data-classification check before activation.
- `edge.map` was an unbounded JSON scalar → now bounded (string→string, 100 entries, 128 chars per key/value). Structural limits only; graph semantics stay the engine's job.

**Correctness** — two of these were caught by *mutating the production code and watching the tests stay green*:
- The **round-trip test was tautological**: the mocked repository assigns by reference, so it compared an object to itself. Gutting the transformer left it passing. It now crosses the transformer/JSON seam against a separately constructed object.
- The **matrix's expert-default row** asserted only `toBeDefined()` — replacing the default graph with `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` kept it 7/7 green. It now asserts real graph content.
- **`schema.graphql` had been hand-authored**, including a *fabricated* description for the JSON scalar and wrong field ordering (~80 lines of divergence from the generator). Regenerated with the repo's own tooling and committed verbatim; this also picks up a pre-existing description drift on `develop`.

Full evidence ledger: `specs/053-generic-prompt-graph/forge-run.md` in the workspace repo.

## Activation (after merge)

Store the payload on a generic persona via `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` — see `docs/prompt-graphs.md`, which covers the walkthrough, the body-of-knowledge precondition, the provider-egress check, and the per-top-level-key merge behaviour (send `promptGraph: null` first for a clean replace).

## What

Adds the sign-in landing the app shell returns to when a browser-based sign-in is required, cancelled or failed.

- `LoginCrdRoute.tsx` — a value-scoped `app_signin` disqualifier over a frozen `APP_SIGN_IN_VALUES` tuple, so `?app_signin=bogus` still redirects rather than rendering an unknown state. Renders a `LoginCardNotice` with the matching `crd-auth` copy, the existing `buildOidcRestartHref` action, and an info/destructive tone
- `LoginCard.tsx` — one optional `tone` prop defaulting to `destructive`, so the existing lockout call site stays byte-identical
- Six locale files gain the `appSignIn` block

No `returnUrl` parameter, no Capacitor or platform detection — client-web only ever *reads* `app_signin`. A review fix also ensures an already-signed-in app user reaching `?app_signin=required` actually lands here instead of being bounced to `/home` by `NotAuthenticatedRoute`.

## Why

The app opens the whole auth chain in a real browser. When that browser leg ends without a session — the user cancelled, or the handoff failed — the shell needs somewhere to land that offers a *correct* restart, not a plain web login in the wrong cookie jar.

## Tests

`pnpm typecheck:native` clean; **8 files / 74 tests** across `src/main/crdPages/auth`, `src/crd/components/auth`, `src/crd/i18n/auth`.

## Workspace feature

## Design in one paragraph

The whole authentication chain runs in a **real browser** (`ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, Chrome Custom Tab on Android), which satisfies every IdP's embedded-WebView policy and keeps Kratos CSRF, Hydra and pre-auth cookies in one consistent jar. The session is handed back into the WebView **once, server-side**, through a single-use ≤60s Redis code redeemed with a verifier in the `X-Alkemio-App-Verifier` request header. **Tokens never leave the server.** App mode is decided at `/login` (not `/callback`) and made sticky in the signed pre-auth cookie — mandatory, because Kratos' `registration.after.oidc` re-enters a *bare* `/api/auth/oidc/login` with no query string, so a query-param-only flag is provably lost on the social sign-up leg. The redirect scheme is **derived** from a frozen host map, not configured, so no infra change ships with this. `returnto-validator.ts` is untouched.

|---|---|
| Triage | routed `spec`; 7 of 9 premise claims confirmed against real code, 2 escalated and then closed by the operator |
| Spec review | attempt 1 stopped at `revise-exhausted` (40→38 findings, 27 blocking both rounds). Re-architected smaller under 4 operator mandates. Attempt 2 converged **23 → 16 → 13 blocking, zero HIGH**; 13 mediums knowingly accepted as tracked spec debt |

| **Live verification** | **`not-applicable` — NO stack was booted and NO acceptance walk was run.** `server/quickstart-services.yml` pins 24 `container_name` values `docker compose -p` cannot namespace, so an isolated stack would stack-conflict or collide with a developer's dev stack. Executed evidence is the per-repo gates plus two in-process supertest integration specs |
| Review funnel | 34 raw → 32 in-diff → 25 confirmed → **14 actionable**, 7 refuted with verbatim source citations |
| Fixes | **13 of 14 fixed**, scoped confirm pass over the fix hunks, **0 regressions** |
| Security verdict | **conditional** on all three repos, with one accepted high (below) |

## ⚠️ Accepted risk — SEC-079-01 (high, operator-attested)

**A malicious Android app squatting the `io.alkem.app` private-use scheme can redeem a full `alkemio_session`** — including a refresh token with `offline_access` — for a victim who holds a live `ory_kratos_session` in Chrome's jar. The PKCE-shaped verifier/challenge binding defeats *interception* of a legitimate flow but gives nothing against a flow **the attacker itself initiated**, because the attacker chose the challenge. Before this change a hostile local app could at most mint a session in Chrome's own jar, which its sandbox cannot read; the handoff converts that into a redeemable bearer credential.

The adjudicator **refused** a proposed downgrade to medium. Accepted by **@bobbykolev** on 2026-09-29 to unblock shipping, tracked as **alkem-io/server#6545**. Narrowing preconditions: the attacker app must be installed; the victim must hold that Chrome Kratos session (a legitimate in-app sign-in clears it); **Android only**, since iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession` is ephemeral. Fixes alkem-io/server#6329

## Root cause

The bot creates every Alkemio room (power level 100) but leaves it once members join, so users never see it. Every member holds power level 50. Synapse lets a sender kick only a target it **strictly** outranks, so in a room nobody can kick anybody. Removing a member (`HandleBatchRemoveMember` → `KickUser`) therefore always failed with `M_FORBIDDEN`: `getIntentForRoom` picked a same-rank member as the kicker.

This PR addresses only cause 1 from the issue (the Matrix-side rejection). Cause 2 (authorization policy never reset on reapply) is already fixed on `server` `develop`.

## Fix

`KickUser` (`internal/infrastructure/matrix/mautrix.go`) now removes a user as follows:

- **Space:** the bot, which stays a member of spaces, kicks as before (`develop` behaviour).
- **Room, target joined, invited or knocking:** the target's own ghost leaves the room (`EnsureRegistered` first). The operator's reason is not attached, since Matrix would record it as the member's own statement.
- **Room, target with no membership** (never joined, e.g. a forum discussion or community updates room, or already left): nothing is sent, and the removal is reported as forbidden (`NOT_ALLOWED`), the same result the old kick returned. No leave event would follow, so reporting success would leave the server waiting for one and the member could never be removed there.

The bot is never brought back into a room, so the timeline never shows "bot joined / bot left". Failures to read the room type or memberships are returned as errors, not treated as success.

Because the fix is inside `KickUser`, every caller gets it: batch removal (group conversations, forum discussions, community updates rooms, cross-L0 space moves), room deletion (`DeleteRoomFully`) and `KickFromSpace`. `MatrixPort` is unchanged.

## Commit history

The branch has three commits, kept as-is:
1. `baf2c6d` made the removed member leave for every batch removal. That returned 403 "not in room" for users who never joined a room.
2. `3d84c6c` kicked with an account that outranks the target, admin-joining the bot when needed. That made the bot visible in the room timeline.
3. `fce20f7` is the approach described above. It keeps the membership check from (2) and drops the bot re-admission.
4. `1fdc532` reports a target with no membership as a failed removal instead of a silent success.

## Behaviour notes

- **Matrix history.** A removed room member shows as "X left", never "X was removed". A voluntary leave (`leaveConversation` goes through the same removal) now reads accurately.
- **Listener.** `listener.go` `handleMembershipEvent` emits the same `leave` event whether the member left or was kicked; the server's `handleRoomMemberUpdated` does not look at who acted.
- **Companion server change** (branch `fix/6329-removed-member-leaves-room`, no PR yet):
  - the group-conversation local-removal fallback always completes;
  - a late leave after a timed-out removal is a no-op;
  - leave events for rooms already deleted are ignored, since room deletion now makes every member really leave.

## Tests

- 6 new adapter tests in `mautrix_intent_test.go`, 10 cases counting subtests:
  - space kick and its error;
  - room leave for join, invite and knock, asserting the target's own intent leaves and no other intent acts or joins;
  - forbidden (`domain.ErrForbidden`) for never-joined and already-left;
  - leave error;
  - read-error propagation.
- The room tests fail against `develop`'s `KickUser`.
- `TestHandleBatchRemoveMember_RemovalRejected`: a rejected removal is returned as a per-room `ErrCodeNotAllowed`, never as a success.
- `KickFromSpace` test fixtures now carry a space `m.room.create`.
- `go test ./...`, `make build` and `make lint` (0 issues) pass. Not verified against a live Synapse.

## Code comments

This PR touches code comments; none reference specs, issues, or PR numbers.

  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-62.md>
- Metalayer rescue for disaster recovery ([#​8408](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8408))
  - The new `$JS.API.META.RESCUE` endpoint can temporarily lower the quorum-needed for the metalayer, in order to facilitate the recovery of a system where nodes have been permanently lost and the metalayer cannot reach quorum
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-61.md>
- Stream backup and restore v2 ([#​7882](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/7882), [#​8584](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8584), [#​8591](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8591), [#​8604](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8604))
  - A new backup format for stream snapshots which reads out per-message rather than per-block
  - The new backup format also now correctly includes non-replicated consumers on follower nodes
  - ADR: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-architecture-and-design/blob/main/adr/ADR-63.md>
- Detect source stream recreation ([#​8384](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8384))
  - The server now detects a source stream being recreated, restarting the sourcing back from the beginning, ensuring new messages are sourced
- Stream source indexing ([#​8282](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8282), [#​8516](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8516), [#​8283](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8283))
  - Restarts and leader changes previously required expensive backward scans through the stream to find the last sourced indices. These are now persisted in an index for instant lookup.
- Domain-prefixed JS API in system account ([#​8429](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8429))
  - When a system account is bridged between the hub and a leaf node, the domain-prefixed JS API can now be used to operate on the leaf node while directly connected to the hub

##### Changed

JetStream

- Streams now have a default limit of 1000 consumers, unless `max_consumers` is specified in the stream config or account limits ([#​8337](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8337), [#​8566](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8566))
  - Applications planning to use a large number of consumers on a stream should configure `max_consumers` in the stream config or account limits to an appropriately high number
  - The server-wide default of 1000 can be overridden by setting `default_max_consumers` in the JetStream limits, or can be disabled by setting to `-1`
  - This limit does not affect existing consumers and will not result in consumer deletions, only the creation of new consumers is prevented
- Sync changes for replicated streams ([#​8447](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8447))
  - When the `sync_interval` is set to `always`, replicated streams now sync their WAL entries but no longer sync upper stream layer writes
  - The synced log allows the stream to recover safely, but removing unnecessary syncs from the upper stream layer dramatically improves performance
  - Non-replicated R1 streams are not affected by this change and will continue to sync at the stream layer as normal
- The `js_raft_delete_range` feature is now enabled by default ([#​8520](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8520))

## What & why

Test coverage for organization email invitations, plus the Space changes that come with them. `workspace#081-org-email-invitations` · Implements alkem-io/client-web#10356

## Changes

- **server-api (vitest it-specs):**
  - The org email invitation matrix (invite, repeat, registered-address path, revoke, permissions).
  - **Registration:** precedence over domain auto-join, conversion carrying the message and language, account-deletion erasure, and US4-AS4 (consumed records never resurrected; needs harness Postgres).
  - **Resend** on Space and Org: throttled, consumed, permission refusals, an admin from another space, an anonymous caller, and revoke + re-invite still throttled.
  - The org email-notification spec.
  - Per-address mail checks replace the global MailSlurper prune.
- **client-web (Playwright):** the persisted walks `organization-email-invitations/` US1, US2, US3 and a US3-AS1 two-row walk, with the test plan.
- **Updated existing specs** to match new semantics:
  - 062 US1-AS6: orgs can now invite by email.
  - Space `invitation-external` and `invitation-subspace-admin`: consumed rows are no longer listed.
- **Fixtures** use reserved domains (`example.com`) for synthetic invitees.

## Running

- Load **`server-api/.env`** for both server-api and the Playwright walks. The root `.env` in a local clone may hold a **different** harness password, and mixing the two registers `admin@alkem.io` with the wrong one.
- The US3 after-window walk needs `PLATFORM_INVITATION_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` set to 30 or less on the server and on the harness. Otherwise it skips, with a reason.
- On a fresh stack with Kratos's HaveIBeenPwned check on, the shared harness password is rejected as breached. Disable that check on the test Kratos.

## Verification (live, isolated stack)

- **Acceptance walks:** 27/27 scenarios across US1–US4, headless Playwright with screenshot evidence. US1-AS5 and US3-AS1 were re-walked after review.
- **Live GraphQL sequence:** 26/26.
- **Regression after review:**
  - test-suites server-api roleset, associates and invitations: 122 passed, 1 skipped. Org email-notification spec: 2/2.
  - Playwright walks: 21/22. The one failure was `us3-as1-two-rows`, an intermittent missed email coinciding with 39 SMTP connection drops to the local MailSlurper sink.
  - Re-run on a fresh stack: 30/30, with the two-row walk 3/3. The resend API spec failed its first attempt and passed on retry; that failure wasn't attributed.
- **Review:** 4 dimensions × 4 repos, including SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security, plus three scoped re-reviews of later fixes. Final security verdict: **pass** on every repo, no security hold.

## Spec

- Workspace spec: [`specs/081-org-email-invitations`](https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/081-org-email-invitations/specs/081-org-email-invitations)

## Tracked residuals (low / info — recorded, not fixed here)

- **Erasure:** account deletion erases email invitations under the account's *current* address only. Rows stored under an earlier address, before an email change, survive.
- **Cooldown:** the create path doesn't check the per-address resend cooldown, so revoke + re-invite is bounded only by the hourly email budget.
- **Redis outage:** the email budget and the resend cooldown both fail open when Redis errors.
- **Logging:**
  - Successful external email dispatches are logged at verbose level only.
  - The notifications service's existing verbose payload log contains the invitee address and message.
- **Retention:** open invitations to people who never register are kept indefinitely.
- **Disclosure:** inviters learn whether an address belongs to a registered account (existing space behaviour, now extended to organization admins and the typed-duplicate echo). `lookup.platformInvitation(ID)` is READ-gated (KG-5).
- **Owner/Admin claims:** an Owner/Admin offer to an outside address is claimed by whoever registers with it. The claim relies on identity-resolve forcing `emailVerified: true` (KG-6).
- **Client permissions:** the client shows Revoke and Resend on email rows without checking the viewer's privileges; the server enforces them.
- **Test coverage:**
  - No live test drives the hourly email budget past its limit; server unit specs cover it.
  - The test-suites generated SDK still has the old resend description.
- **Space email (not touched, frozen):** it greets account-less recipients with "Hi ," and shows a dead notification-preferences link (KG-9).
- **Address length:** the input allows 512 characters but the record allows 128 (KG-2).

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.
